paper.title: Language Generation with Feedback: Queries and Mistakes
paper.summary: Characterizes generation with mistake and query feedback through countable inner covers, compares element- and set-valued models, proves countable-union and zero-example consequences, establishes robustness to eventually correct feedback, and studies no-feedback set versus element generation.

formalization_scope.summary: The semantic/classical statements of Theorems 3.1--3.4 and Corollaries 3.6--3.8 are fully formalized through stable Results/Overview wrappers. For Theorem 3.9, the set-to-element direction is fully formalized and the reverse is formalized under the self-locking premise used in Appendix A.6.1; a kernel-checked counterexample exposes the Lemma A.8 proof gap. For Theorem 3.10, Appendix Theorems A.9, A.12, and A.13 are fully formalized independently, while A.10 and the source proof of A.11 remain deferred because they use unrestricted Theorem 3.9.
specializations: The source's countable universe and infinite-language assumptions are explicit as Countable alpha, Infinite alpha, and a class-wide infinitude hypothesis.
A countable inner cover is represented by an explicit sequence of infinite subsets; repetitions are allowed and do not change the property.
Theorem 3.3 uses the source's literal universe Nat and an equivalent zero-based div/mod partition into three-point blocks; this only reindexes the paper's positive-integer blocks.

Theorem 3.4 uses a source-timed semantic interface with one membership query per round, rather than the older auxiliary square-batch or pre-sample query models retained elsewhere in the paper directory.
Corollary 3.7 uses interfaces that literally omit the positive-example input rather than supplying a dummy presentation.

Corollary 3.8 quantifies over arbitrary example streams and external Boolean streams that become correct after a finite prefix. Lean uses an infinitely repeated cover and queried-point removal as an alternative semantic robustification to the appendix's finite-expansion construction.

Theorem 3.9 uses the repository's generic no-feedback element and infinite-set generation interfaces. The set-to-element projection is unconditional; the checked element-to-set self-simulation assumes the appendix's explicit per-presentation self-locking normal form.
Appendix Theorem A.9 is proved for an arbitrary nonempty countable example type by reducing a finite inner cover to P02's finite union of infinite upward cones.
For Appendix Theorem A.12, Lean proves the stronger reusable statement for every countable UUS class over a countably infinite universe, then exposes a concrete singleton-class source wrapper.
Appendix Theorem A.13 follows the source's explicit pairwise-disjoint vertical fibers on Nat times Nat; the generator is semantic and uses classical fresh selection.
The development is classical semantic mathematics and makes no extracted-executability, runtime, or query-complexity claim.
gaps: The unrestricted element-to-set direction of no-feedback Theorem 3.9 is deliberately deferred: Appendix Lemma A.8's self-locking inference is false as stated for sequence-sensitive generators, although this does not refute the headline equivalence. No further proof search or counterexample construction is planned unless a corrected source statement or independent new proof becomes available.
Theorem 3.10 / Appendix Theorem A.10 and the source proof of A.11 are deliberately deferred because they invoke the unrestricted Theorem 3.9 conversion; A.9, A.12, and A.13 are fully formalized.
No P27 claim currently has a completed human statement-correspondence audit; the locally inspected source snapshot is checksum-pinned, but the statement comparison remains AI-assisted.

claims.title: Element-valued mistake feedback is characterized by countable inner covers
claims.statement_summary: A class of infinite languages over a countable universe is generatable with truthful element-valued mistake feedback if and only if it has a countable inner cover.

claims.title: No-feedback set and element generation are equivalent
claims.statement_summary: A language class is generatable in the no-feedback infinite-set model if and only if it is generatable in the ordinary no-feedback element model.

source_assessment.notes: The set-to-element direction is sound. The source's element-to-set proof depends on Appendix Lemma A.8, whose per-presentation self-locking inference is refuted by a kernel-checked sequence-sensitive counterexample. This identifies a proof gap but does not refute the headline equivalence, which may admit a different proof or a valid generator normal form.

formalization.notes: Lean fully proves the set-to-element direction and the element-to-set self-simulation under the exact self-locking premise used by the appendix. The unrestricted reverse direction is not claimed and further proof or counterexample work is deliberately deferred pending a corrected source statement or independent new argument.

components.summary: Every no-feedback infinite-set generator yields an ordinary element generator by choosing an output point.
An ordinary no-feedback element generator satisfying the appendix's self-locking normal form yields an infinite-set generator by self-simulation.
Every ordinary no-feedback element generator can be put in the required self-locking form or converted to an infinite-set generator by another argument.

lean_links.notes: Core's generic projection chooses one member of each eventually correct infinite set output.
The construction iterates a freshened element generator on its own hypothetical outputs; correctness follows once the observed history is self-locking for all finite target continuations.

relations.notes: The source proof of the element-to-set direction invokes Appendix Lemma A.8; the registered lemma card records why that proof obligation is not available as stated.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audits for both maintained Theorem 3.9 endpoints.

claims.title: Successful fresh generators self-lock along every presentation
claims.statement_summary: Appendix Lemma A.8 claims that after enforcing fresh outputs, every successful sequence generator has a self-locking prefix along each fixed presentation, stable under every finite target continuation.

source_assessment.notes: Lean gives a fresh generator for a singleton infinite target class that makes at most one error on every stream, hence succeeds on every presentation, but whose canonical target presentation has no self-locking prefix. This refutes the lemma's unrestricted inference for ordered sequence-sensitive generators; named human source-correspondence review remains outstanding.

formalization.notes: The source lemma is not maintained as a theorem. The linked declaration packages a direct kernel-checked counterexample and therefore contributes no positive coverage.

lean_links.notes: Pairwise prefix-incomparable spike histories ensure at most one invalid output on every stream while placing a bad finite continuation after every prefix of the chosen presentation.

relations.notes: The source uses Lemma A.8 in the element-to-set proof of Theorem 3.9; its failure explains why the unrestricted reverse implication is not claimed.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for the Appendix Lemma A.8 counterexample wrapper.

claims.title: Finite and countable inner covers bound no-feedback generation
claims.statement_summary: Theorem 3.10 gives finite-inner-cover sufficiency, countable-inner-cover necessity, strictness examples for both bounds, and an example satisfying the countable necessary condition.

source_assessment.notes: Appendix Theorems A.9, A.12, and A.13 are independently checked. The source proof of A.10 invokes unrestricted Theorem 3.9, and the source proof of A.11 then invokes A.10; those proof routes inherit the Appendix Lemma A.8 gap. No issue is identified in the three maintained components, and no claim is made that the remaining two statements are false.

formalization.notes: Three of the five Appendix components are fully formalized through stable Overview wrappers. A.10 and the source route to A.11 are deliberately deferred together with unrestricted Theorem 3.9.

components.summary: A finite inner cover suffices for no-feedback generation in the limit.
No-feedback generation in the limit implies the existence of a countable inner cover.
A countable inner cover does not suffice for no-feedback generation in the limit.
There exists a no-feedback-generatable class with a countable inner cover.
There exists a no-feedback-generatable class with no finite inner cover.

lean_links.notes: The original class is embedded into the finite union of upward cones above its cover members, and P02's finite-cone generator is restricted back to the class.
The public wrapper supplies a singleton witness; the implementation module also proves the source proof's stronger reusable statement for every countable UUS class.
The first observed pair identifies the source's vertical fiber; classical fresh selection supplies later outputs, and a finite-coordinate argument rules out finite inner covers.

relations.notes: The maintained A.9 proof is an upward-cone specialization of P02's finite-cover generation result.
The stronger reusable A.12 lemma obtains countable-class generation from P02's nonuniform characterization.
The two deferred components are exactly the parts whose source proofs use unrestricted Theorem 3.9 directly or through A.10.
